questions.title: Length and Boundary Characters
questions.description:
Read one word and report its size and boundary letters: print the number of characters in the word, then its first character, then its last character, each on its own line.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word without spaces.

Output Format:
Line 1: the length of the word.
Line 2: the first character.
Line 3: the last character.

Constraints:
1 <= length of word <= 1000, word contains only lowercase letters
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of word <= 1000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Case Conversion of a Word
questions.description:
Read one word and print it twice: first entirely in uppercase, then entirely in lowercase, each on its own line.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word without spaces (letters only, any mix of cases).

Output Format:
Line 1: the word in uppercase.
Line 2: the word in lowercase.

Constraints:
1 <= length of word <= 1000, letters only
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of word <= 1000, letters only

questions.title: Extract a Substring by Index
questions.description:
Read a word and two indices start and end. Print the part of the word that begins at index start (included) and stops at index end (not included). Remember that substring(2, 5) gives the characters at indices 2, 3 and 4.

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated values: the word, then the integer start, then the integer end.

Output Format:
Print one line: the extracted substring.

Constraints:
0 <= start < end <= length of word, word has no spaces
questions.inputconstrains: 0 <= start < end <= length of word

questions.title: Frequency of a Target Character
questions.description:
Read a word and a target character. Count how many times the target character appears anywhere in the word and print that count.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated values: the word (no spaces) and the target character.

Output Format:
Print one line: the number of occurrences of the target character.

Constraints:
1 <= length of word <= 1000, word and target contain only lowercase letters
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of word <= 1000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Replace All Occurrences of a Letter
questions.description:
Read a word, an original character and a replacement character. Print the word with every occurrence of the original character replaced by the replacement character. Use the replace method that takes two characters (no regular expressions).

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated values: the word, the character to replace, and the replacement character.

Output Format:
Print one line: the modified word.

Constraints:
1 <= length of word <= 1000, all characters are lowercase letters
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of word <= 1000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Which Word Comes First
questions.description:
Read two words and decide their dictionary (lexicographic) order using compareTo. Print first if the first word comes earlier in dictionary order, second if the second word comes earlier, or equal if the words are identical.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated words, each without spaces.

Output Format:
Print one line: first, second or equal.

Constraints:
1 <= length of each word <= 100, words contain only lowercase letters
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each word <= 100, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Username Validator
questions.description:
A signup form must reject weak usernames. A username is valid when its length is between 6 and 12 (both included) AND it contains at least one underscore character. Read the username and print valid or invalid.

Input Format:
A single line containing one username without spaces (letters, digits and underscores only).

Output Format:
Print one line: valid if the username passes both rules, otherwise invalid.

Constraints:
1 <= length of username <= 100
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of username <= 100, letters digits and underscores only

questions.title: Product Code Formatter
questions.description:
A warehouse scanner emits product codes wrapped in stray spaces. Clean the raw line by trimming leading and trailing spaces, then print the code in uppercase. Spaces inside the code (if any) must be kept.

Input Format:
A single line containing the raw product code, possibly with leading and trailing spaces (read the whole line).

Output Format:
Print one line: the trimmed code converted to uppercase.

Constraints:
1 <= length of raw line <= 200
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of raw line <= 200

questions.title: Initials From a Full Name
questions.description:
An email generator builds a person's initials from their full name. Read the full name (words separated by single spaces) and print the first character of every word joined together.

Input Format:
A single line containing 2 to 5 words separated by single spaces, each word starting with a letter.

Output Format:
Print one line: the initials, one character per word in order.

Constraints:
2 <= number of words <= 5, 1 <= length of each word <= 20, letters only
questions.inputconstrains: 2 <= number of words <= 5, letters only

questions.title: Vehicle Plate Number Checker
questions.description:
A parking system accepts only plates of the form two uppercase letters followed by four digits, for example TN0924. Read the plate and print valid when it is exactly 6 characters long, starts with two uppercase letters and ends with four digits; otherwise print invalid.

Input Format:
A single line containing one plate token without spaces (letters and digits only).

Output Format:
Print one line: valid or invalid.

Constraints:
1 <= length of plate <= 10
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of plate <= 10, letters and digits only

questions.title: Mirror Word Builder
questions.description:
A puzzle app shows mirror words by flipping each word backwards. Read a word and print it reversed by building the result manually with a character array: copy the characters into a new array from last to first. Do not use StringBuilder or any built-in reverse utility.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word without spaces.

Output Format:
Print one line: the word reversed.

Constraints:
1 <= length of word <= 100000, lowercase letters only
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of word <= 100000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Palindrome Phrase Checker
questions.description:
A word game checks whether a phrase is a palindrome while ignoring case and ignoring every character that is not a letter (spaces, digits and punctuation are skipped). Read one whole line, keep only the letters converted to lowercase, and decide whether that cleaned text reads the same forwards and backwards using two pointers.

Input Format:
A single line containing the phrase, possibly with spaces and punctuation (read the whole line).

Output Format:
Print palindrome when the cleaned text is a palindrome, otherwise print not a palindrome.

Constraints:
1 <= length of line <= 1000, line contains at least one letter
questions.input1: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama!
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of line <= 1000, at least one letter

questions.title: Anagram Check With Count Arrays
questions.description:
A crossword generator must verify that two words are anagrams: they use exactly the same letters with the same counts. Read two lowercase words and compare their letter counts using two integer arrays of size 26 (one slot per letter a to z). Do not sort the words and do not use maps.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated words, each without spaces.

Output Format:
Print anagram when the words are anagrams of each other, otherwise print not anagram.

Constraints:
1 <= length of each word <= 1000, lowercase letters only
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each word <= 1000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Capitalize the Title
questions.description:
A blogging platform stores every title in lowercase and needs it displayed in Title Case: the first letter of every word becomes uppercase and every other letter becomes lowercase. Read one whole line of words separated by single spaces and print the converted title by rewriting the characters of a character array in place.

Input Format:
A single line containing words separated by single spaces, letters only (read the whole line).

Output Format:
Print one line: the title where each word starts with an uppercase letter and all remaining letters are lowercase.

Constraints:
1 <= length of line <= 1000, letters and single spaces only
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of line <= 1000, letters and single spaces only

questions.title: Most Frequent Letter
questions.description:
A cipher tool studies letter usage. Read a word of lowercase letters and find the most frequent letter. If several letters occur the same maximum number of times, choose the smallest letter alphabetically. Print the letter on the first line and its count on the second line.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word without spaces.

Output Format:
Line 1: the winning letter.
Line 2: how many times it occurs.

Constraints:
1 <= length of word <= 1000, lowercase letters only
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of word <= 1000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Sentence Statistics Line
questions.description:
A reading app shows quick statistics for a sentence: the number of words, the number of vowels and the number of consonants. Words are maximal runs of letters separated by spaces (a, e, i, o, u count as vowels, both cases). Scan the line character by character with charAt instead of splitting it.

Input Format:
A single line containing letters and single spaces, with at least one word (read the whole line).

Output Format:
Line 1: number of words.
Line 2: number of vowels.
Line 3: number of consonants.

Constraints:
1 <= length of line <= 1000, letters and single spaces only
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of line <= 1000, letters and single spaces only

questions.title: Run-Length Encoding of a Word
questions.description:
A compression module encodes test words using run-length encoding: each maximal run of one repeated character is replaced by the character followed by the length of the run, and a run of length 1 is written as just the character with no count. For example aaabb becomes a3b2 and abbc becomes ab2c. Read the word and print its encoded form, building the answer with StringBuilder.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word without spaces.

Output Format:
Print one line: the run-length encoded word.

Constraints:
1 <= length of word <= 100000, lowercase letters only
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of word <= 100000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Longest Word in a Sentence
questions.description:
A typing tutor highlights the longest word of a sentence. Read one whole line of words separated by single spaces, split it with the plain single-space literal, and find the longest word. If several words share the maximum length, use the first of them. Print the longest word and then its length.

Input Format:
A single line containing words separated by single spaces, letters only (read the whole line).

Output Format:
Line 1: the longest word.
Line 2: its length.

Constraints:
1 <= length of line <= 100000, letters and single spaces only
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of line <= 100000, letters and single spaces only

questions.title: Cancel Adjacent Duplicates
questions.description:
A text cleaner cancels pairs of equal adjacent characters repeatedly, like removing dominoes: whenever two neighboring characters are equal, both disappear and their neighbors join. For example azxxzy becomes ay, and abba cancels completely. Read a word and simulate the process with a character array used as a buffer (no Deque or Stack classes). Print the final word, or EMPTY when nothing remains.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word without spaces.

Output Format:
Print one line: the cleaned word, or EMPTY when the cleaned word is empty.

Constraints:
1 <= length of word <= 100000, lowercase letters only
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of word <= 100000, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Rotation Check
questions.description:
A cryptography workshop studies circular shifts of words. Word s2 is a rotation of word s1 when s2 can be produced by moving some prefix of s1 to its end; for example cdab is a rotation of abcd but acdb is not, and an identical word counts as a rotation (shift of zero). Check it by testing whether s2 appears inside s1 concatenated with itself, with equal lengths required.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated words, each without spaces.

Output Format:
Print yes when s2 is a rotation of s1, otherwise print no.

Constraints:
1 <= length of each word <= 100000, lowercase letters only
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of each word <= 100000, lowercase letters only
